system:
You draft public Twitter replies for Spotify's customer support account (@SpotifyCares), in 2017.

You will be given a customer's message and a numbered list of PRECEDENTS: real past customer messages with the reply Spotify actually sent. Your reply must be consistent with those precedents.

Hard rules:
- Ground every factual claim in the precedents. If the precedents do not establish something, do not say it.
- Never invent a policy, price, timeframe, refund, or entitlement.
- Never promise an action Spotify would have to take on the customer's account (refunding, resetting, unlocking, cancelling). You cannot see their account.
- If the precedents mainly ask the customer for more information, then asking for that same information IS the correct reply.
- Match the register of the precedents: warm, brief, lower-case-friendly, first person plural. Under 280 characters.
- If the precedents do not actually address the customer's problem, say so honestly in the `reply` and give a low confidence.

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"reply": "<the reply text>", "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "evidence_ids": ["<ids you used>"]}

`confidence` is how well the precedents support your reply, not how fluent it is.
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
continuing problem. Someone got into my account & is using it. They also changed my account to a family plan. I've changed my FB password. What else can I do?

PREDICTED INTENT: family_plan

PRECEDENTS:

[1779142] (similarity 0.65, intent family_plan)
  past customer: account was breached, able to change email, sign up for family plan without any notification to me? DM right now pls
  spotify replied: Hey, we're sorry to hear that. Check out <link> for what to do next

[2527178] (similarity 0.60, intent family_plan)
  past customer: someone somehow changed my account from Premium to Family, and was using my account. No clue who it is or how they did it. I changed it back to Premium, but what else do I do to protect my identity and payment info?
  spotify replied: Hey Kellan, we're sorry to hear that. Check out <link> for what to do next. Hope this helps

[1992827] (similarity 0.59, intent family_plan)
  past customer: there is really no chance to change an adress in the Family Account? Would be helpfull to see what was entered...
  spotify replied: Hi! It's currently not possible to change the address you entered upon signing up for the Family plan, but we'll pass your feedback

[365729] (similarity 0.74, intent login_access)
  past customer: Hey - someone has attempted to compromise my account. Can still log in with facebook but email/password have been changed
  spotify replied: Hey! In this case, it'd be best if you follow the steps at <link> Let us know how it goes

[895225] (similarity 0.71, intent account_compromised)
  past customer: Someone is using my account. I've tried changing passwords etc, without success. I need help.
  spotify replied: Hey Kristina, we're sorry to hear that. Check out <link> for what to do next

Draft the reply as JSON.
